questions.question: Find the value of tan (−1125°).
questions.solution:
**Formula used:**

Tan (- θ) = - tan θ 

Tan (360 + θ) = tan θ 

**Calculation:**

Tan (−1125°) = - tan 1125°

⇒ - tan 1125° = - tan {(360 × 3) + 45)

⇒ - tan {1080 + 45} = - tan 45° = - 1

**∴ The correct answer is -1.**

questions.question: If RP and RQ are two tangents to a circle with centre O such that ∠POQ = 120°, where P and Q are the points on the circle and R is a point outside the circle then ∠PRQ is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

RP and RQ are the two tangents of a circle.

∠POQ = 120°

**Concept used:**

The tangent makes a right angle with the radius of a circle at the point of contact.

The sum of all angles of a quadrilateral = 360°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9582cbb3bd8c42532220dc26d56427522814752885e075b9fc1c3995b13695e0.png] 

In the figure:

OP ⊥ PR and OQ ⊥ RQ

∠OPR = ∠OQR = 90°

In quadrilateral POQR

⇒ ∠OPR + ∠OQR + ∠POQ + ∠PRQ = 360

⇒​ 90 + 90 + 120 + ∠PRQ = 360

⇒ ∠PRQ = (360 - 300) = 60°

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

questions.question: The length, breadth and height of a hall are 10 m, 20 m and 15 m respectively. Find the cost of whitewashing the walls of the inside of the hall and ceiling at the rate of Rs. 10.20/m²
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of the hall = 10 m

Breadth of the hall = 20 m

Height of the hall = 15 m

Rate of whitewashing of walls = Rs.10.20/m²

**Formula used:**

Area of rectangle = L × B

Area of four walls = 2 × H × (L + B)

Where, L = length; B = breadth; H = height

**Calculation:**

The total area of the hall = Area of four walls + area of the ceiling

⇒ 2 × H × (L + B) + (L × B)

⇒ 2 × 15 × (10 + 20) + (10 × 20)

⇒ 2 × 15 × 30 + 200

⇒ 900 + 200 = 1100 m²

Total cost = 1100 × 10.20 = Rs.11220

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.11220.**

questions.question: If p + q + r = pqr = {1 over p} + {1 over q} + {1 over r} = 1, then find p³ + q³ + r³.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

p + q + r = p × q × r = {1 over p} + {1 over q} + {1 over r} = 1

**Formula used:**

(a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2 × (ab + bc + ca)

a³ + b³ + c³ = (a + b + c) × (a² + b² + c² - ab - bc - ca) + 3abc

**Calculation:**

 {1 over p} + {1 over q} + {1 over r} = 1

⇒ (qr + pr + pq)/pqr = 1

⇒ (qr + pr + pq) = 1

p + q + r = 1

squaring both sides:

⇒ (p + q + r)² = 1²

⇒ p2 + q2 + r2 + 2 × (pq + qr + pr) = 1

⇒ p2 + q2 + r2 + 2 × 1 = 1

⇒ p2 + q2 + r2 = 1 - 2 = - 1

p3 + q3 + r3 = (p + q + r) × (p2 + q2 + r2 - pq - qr - pr) + 3pqr

⇒ 1 × (- 1 - 1) + 3

⇒ - 2 + 3 = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

questions.question: Mona purchased two sets of jewellery for Rs. 4,000 each. She sold these sets of jewellery, gaining 8% on one and losing 6% on the other. Calculate her total loss or gain in this whole transaction.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When Cost Price (CP) is same for both items:

Net Gain/Loss = Total Profit Value − Total Loss Value

⇒ Net Gain/Loss = (8% of 4000) − (6% of 4000)

⇒ Net Gain/Loss = 2% of 4000 = 80

⇒ Since the result is positive, it is a gain of Rs. 80.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 80 gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

CP of each jewellery set = Rs. 4000

Profit% on 1st set = 8%

Loss% on 2nd set = 6%

**Formula Used:**

Profit or Loss = CP × (Profit or Loss % / 100)

 Transaction Breakdown
 
 
 Set 1: CP = 4000
 

 +8% Gain
 
 
 Set 2: CP = 4000
 

 −6% Loss
 
 
• 
 Total Result = Gain (320) − Loss (240) = Rs. 80
 
 
 
 

 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total CP = 4000 + 4000 = Rs. 8000

⇒ Profit on the first jewellery set = 4000 × (8 / 100) = Rs. 320

⇒ Loss on the second jewellery set = 4000 × (6 / 100) = Rs. 240

⇒ Total Gain/Loss = 320 − 240 = +80

⇒ Since the net value is positive, it is a gain of Rs. 80.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 80 gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Case of Same Cost Price (CP)

If two items are bought at the same CP, the net profit or loss percent is simply the arithmetic average of individual profit/loss percentages: Net % = (P1% ± L2%) / 2.

Case of Same Selling Price (SP)

If two items are sold at the same SP, one at x% profit and another at x% loss, there is always a net loss of (x² / 100)%.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100 | Loss % = (Loss / CP) × 100. Profit and loss are always calculated on the Cost Price unless specified otherwise.</p

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 99?
questions.solution:
**Concept used:**

If a number is divisible by 9 and 11 then the number is divisible by 99.

Divisibility rule of 9:

If the sum of the digits is divisible by 9, then the number is divisible by 9.

Divisibility rule of 11:

If the difference between the sum of odd place and even place digits is either 0 or a multiple of 11,

then the number is divisible by 11. 

**Calculation:**

We need to check it by options:

Option 1:

Number = 31548

The sum of digits = 3 + 1 + 5 + 4 + 8 = 21

21 is not divisible by 9. So the number is not divisible by 9

and the number is also not divisible by 99.

Option 2:

Number = 60687

The sum of digits = 6 + 0 + 6 + 8 + 7 = 27

27 is divisible by 9. So the number is divisible by 9.

The sum of odd place digits = 6 + 6 + 7 = 19

The sum of even place digits = 0 + 8 = 8

Difference between sum of odd and even place digits = 19 - 8 = 11 

11 is divisible by 11. So the number is divisible by 11.

and the number is also divisible by 99.

**∴ The correct option is 2.**

questions.question: A family income is Rs. 35,000 in a month. The family spends the income on various expenditures, viz., food, health, education, entertainment, and rent. After incurring all the expenditures, 8% is saved every month. The expenditure on health is 50% more than that of food. While food is three times of the expenditure on entertainment, the expenditure on health is half of the expenditure on education. The expenditure on rent is one-third of the combined expenditure on food, health and education. How much expenditure (in Rs.) is incurred on education?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The monthly income of the family = Rs.35000

Saving after expenditure = 35000 × 8% = 2800

Expenditure = (35000 - 2800) = Rs.32200

Expenditure on food : expenditure on health = 100 : 150 = 2 : 3

Expenditure on food : expenditure on entertainment = 3 : 1

Expenditure on health : expenditure on education = 1 : 2

Expenditure on rent : combined expenditure of (food + health + education) = 1 : 3

**Concept used:**

A : B = P : Q; B : C = R : S

A : B : C = PR : QR : QS

**Calculation**:

Exp. on food : exp. on health : exp. on entertainment : exp. on education = 6 : 9 : 2 : 18

Exp. on rent : combined exp. of (food + health + education) = (1 : 3) × 11 = 11 : 33

Exp. on food : exp. on health : exp. on entertainment : exp. on education : exp. on rent = 6 : 9 : 2 : 18 : 11

Now, (6 + 9 + 2 + 18 + 11) units = 46 units = 32200

⇒ 1 unit = 32200/46 = Rs.700

Exp. on education = 18 units = 700 × 18 = Rs.12600

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.12600.**

Rs. 8,500 becomes Rs. 11,050 in 6 years at a certain rate of simple interest. If the rate becomes 1.8 times of itself, the amount of the same principal in 5 years will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs.8500

Time = 6 years

Amount = Rs.11050

**Formula used:**

Amount = S.I + P

S.I = (P × R × T)/100

Where, P = principal; T = time; R = rate

**Calculation: **

S.I for 6 years = 11050 - 8500 = Rs.2550

Rate = (S.I × 100)/(P × T)

⇒ (2550 × 100)/(8500 × 6)

⇒ 425/85 = 5%

New rate % = 5 × 1.8 = 9%

S.I = (P × R × T)/100

⇒ (8500 × 9 × 5)/100

⇒ 85 × 9 × 5 = Rs.3825

Amount = 8500 + 3825 = Rs.12325

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.12325.**
